next_step: Finalize Dedicated POC SOW, confirm peering window and canary traffic allocation
notes: Account overview: mid-market B2B SaaS (user onboarding/product analytics). Heavy emphasis on fast in-app support and semantic search for docs.
Initial interest triggered by hosted API trial: good dev velocity, but forecasting cost at scale -> exploring Dedicated for predictable unit economics.
AE quote: 'Need predictable p99s and an easy canary path to Dedicated; procurement will want clear rollback criteria.'
Primary technical contacts: VP Eng (Leah Barnes), Staff ML Eng (Ravi Menon). Security lead: Camille Ortiz.
Security asks: SOC2 + KMS integration, ability to restrict model weights from leaving VPC (routing assurance), retention controls for logs and prompts.
Current plan: pilot on Hosted API for two months, then 6-week Dedicated POC if latency/cost targets justify migration.

POC acceptance criteria (agreement v1): p99 latency < 250ms for short chat (~512 tokens), error rate < 0.5%, model output quality parity (human eval) within 3% degradation, token cost target < $0.0009 per token.
Canary strategy discussed: start with 5-10% traffic to Dedicated pool, shadowing enabled, then increase to 30% after 72h with SLA monitoring. Progressive ramp with rollback triggers.

Fallback routing: primary route to Dedicated (low-latency variant), automatic fallback to Hosted API model variant if Dedicated capacity exhausted or latency SLA breached. Region failover: primary us-east, failover eu-west for persistence-sensitive workloads is allowed only after DR tests.
Model variant plan: serve quantized 4-bit variant in Dedicated for cost/perf; keep FP16 hosted variant as fallback for quality-critical queries. A/B tags for user cohorts during canary.
Rollback triggers defined: sustained p95>300ms for 15 minutes, error spikes >1% for 5 minutes, or automated quality regression detected by eval harness (ROI metric drop >4%).
Network: customer needs guidance on VPC peering and NAT rules; engineering requested exact CIDR ranges and peering maintenance window.
Pricing: SE ran estimate; preliminary committed capacity proposal sent (see pricing deck). Procurement asked for monthly and annual committed options and overage formulas.
Next tactical items: SOW draft for 6-week Dedicated POC, schedule peering window, security questionnaire completion (SOC2 evidence), confirm acceptance criteria and monitoring dashboard metrics.
Quote from VP Eng: 'If the Dedicated POC can show 30% lower per-token cost while keeping latency stable, we'll push to procurement.'
